title: Perseus: The Golden Shower
subtitle: A prophecy dodged, a chest set adrift, and a boy raised by fishermen

main.author: Pseudo-Apollodorus

main.locator: Library 2.4.1, Acrisius, Danae, and the chest
main.excerpt: putting his daughter with the child in a chest, he cast it into the sea. The chest was washed ashore on Seriphus, and Dictys took up the boy and reared him

narrativeBlocks.title: A king hears his death
narrativeBlocks.body: Acrisius, king of Argos, asks the oracle how he will die. The answer: at the hand of his daughter's son. He has no son — only a daughter, Danae. So he seals her in a bronze chamber where no man can reach her.

narrativeBlocks.title: Zeus arrives as gold
narrativeBlocks.body: Walls don't stop gods. Zeus comes to Danae as a shower of gold pouring through the roof, and she conceives Perseus. Acrisius refuses to believe the father is a god — and now faces the dilemma prophecy always creates: kill the child and risk the gods' wrath, or keep him and risk the oracle.

narrativeBlocks.title: The chest in the sea
narrativeBlocks.body: His solution is a middle cruelty: mother and infant sealed in a wooden chest and thrown into the sea — let the waves, not his hand, do the killing. The chest drifts to the island of Seriphus, where the fisherman Dictys takes the child in and raises him.

narrativeBlocks.title: Growing up unwanted
narrativeBlocks.body: Perseus grows up on Seriphus while King Polydectes — Dictys's brother — falls in love with Danae, who wants nothing to do with him. The king's problem: her grown son stands in the way.

narrativeBlocks.title: The impossible dodge
narrativeBlocks.body: Like Oedipus's story (week 7), this is a prophecy tale: every move to escape the oracle manufactures it. Acrisius's chest doesn't prevent his death — it just ensures the grandson arrives with every reason to be extraordinary.

quiz.prompt: Why does Acrisius imprison Danae in a bronze chamber?

choices.text: She refuses to marry the king he chose
She is punished for worshipping Zeus
An oracle says her son will kill him — sealing her away is his attempt to prevent the child existing
He wants to hide her from pirates

quiz.explanation: The prophecy targets the grandson; the chamber is the grandfather's evasive move.

quiz.prompt: How do Danae and infant Perseus survive Acrisius?

choices.text: They escape to Crete by ship
A temple shelters them from the king
Zeus hides them in the bronze chamber
He seals them in a chest and casts it into the sea — it washes ashore on Seriphus where Dictys raises the boy

quiz.explanation: The sea-chest is the second great 'exposed infant' image in Greek myth — and Perseus is raised a fisherman's son.
